case_name: Mohamed Masthan v Society, Congregation, Bros., S. Heart and Another
respondent:
Society, Congregation, Bros., S. Heart and Another
Supreme Court of India

10 March 2006
Appeal (civil) 1617 of 2006 [Arising out of SLP (C) No. 20291 of 2004]
The Judgment was delivered by : S. B. Sinha, J.
Leave granted.
1. The properties in question are said to be belonging to the Society of Congregation of the Brothers of the Sacred Heart. Brother Lawrance, who was then Superior General of the First Respondent-Society (Society) transferred 8 acres and 44 cents of land to one Siluvai Rajan by a deed of sale dated 18.10.1979. According to the Society, the said sale was illegal. After the death of the said purchaser, his wife sold the property to her sister Juliet Mary, Second Respondent herein by a deed of sale dated 23.7.1986. The First Respondent filed a suit against the Second Respondent in the Court of District Munsif, Tirunelveli which was marked as OS No. 1220 of 1987 praying for declaration of title and possession and consequential injunction. facts: The properties in question are said to be belonging to the Society of Congregation of the Brothers of the Sacred Heart.
Brother Lawrance, who was then Superior General of the First Respondent-Society (Society) transferred 8 acres and 44 cents of land to one Siluvai Rajan by a deed of sale dated 18.10.1979.
The Second Respondent filed a suit against the Society for a declaration that the aforementioned consent decree passed in OS No. 1220 of 1987 was null and void.
The Appellant filed a suit for specific performance of the contract in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Tirunelveli being OS No. 140 of 2003.
The First Respondent contends that they are still in possession.
The Second Respondent entered into a purported agreement for sale with the Appellant herein on or about 1.10.2002.
issues: Whether the decree passed in OS No. 140 of 2003 was collusive or not.
Whether the First Respondent is entitled to execute the decree and take possession of the suit property.
Whether the consent decree passed in OS No. 1220 of 1987 has been set aside.
petitioner_arguments: The Appellant filed a suit for specific performance of the contract in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Tirunelveli being OS No. 140 of 2003.
The Appellant raised a short question in support of this appeal.
Mr. V. Krishna Murthy, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Appellant raised a short question in support of this appeal.
respondent_arguments: The Second Respondent filed a suit against the Society for a declaration that the aforementioned consent decree passed in OS No. 1220 of 1987 was null and void.
Mr. P.S. Mishra, learned senior counsel appearing on behalf of the Respondent submitted that as the First Respondent continued to be in possession of the suit property.
court_reasoning: The High Court rightly went into the question as regards legality or otherwise of the decree passed in the said OS No. 140 of 2003.

The Appellant and the Second Respondent herein had entered into the said purported agreement for sale dated 1.10.2002 only in an attempt to get rid of the compromise decree dated 27.4.1989 passed in OS No. 1220 of 1987.
holding: The High Court was not correct in dealing with the question as to whether the decree passed in OS No. 140 of 2003 was collusive or not.
Both OS No. 381 of 2003 and OS No. 641 of 2003 are directed to be tried jointly by a competent court.
